comments.author: blaze33
comments.why: Zimbardo's past, present, future time orientations
comments.text: Instead of the linear, multi-active and cyclic times paradigm, another approach I found interesting is the one proposed by Philip Zimbardo neatly presented in this video: [VIDEO] It presents individuals as being either past, present or future oriented. Apparently, the closer we are to the equator the more present-oriented we tend to be (because there are less seasonal changes).

comments.author: watmough
comments.story: What a toddler can tell you about the future of media
comments.text: See also this video entitled 'The Secret Powers of Time', posted on twitter by Jeff Atwood. [VIDEO] I have to profess some interest in this, since my own 1-month old will likely grow up with the same iPhones, iPads etc., as the toddler in the article. The most worrying thing, is how the heck can kids raised on new media, Apps and books that talk, ever hope to even tolerate sitting in a classroom enjoying a traditional education? I dread to think of the overhaul that is needed and coming to education.
